subject: english
question:
Select the correct idiom that can substitute the italicised group of words in the given sentence.

Soma has *made a mess* of her financial affairs.

options.text: made a mountain out of a molehill

solution:
The correct answer is **'Option 3'.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The given phrase "Soma has made a mess of her financial affairs" can be replaced by the idiom** "made a hash of," **meaning to make a complete mess of something (बिलकुल गड़बड़ कर देना).

Therefore, the **correct answer** is: **'Made a hash of'.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Option 1:** "Made up one’s mind"** means to make a decision (निश्चय कर लेना).
 
• Option 2: **"Made a mountain out of a molehill"** means to make a small problem seem much bigger (छोटी सी बात को बड़ा बना देना).
 
• Option 4: **"Made both ends meet"** means to manage one's money so that one's income equals one's expenses (गुजारा करना).

3d:Ta96,
The correct answer is 'Option 1'.</str
